messages.subject: d and e parameters
parts:
Dear Nick

I had a bit of a basic question about the precise nature of the d and e parameters. In your publications/thesis you describe these as rates of range addition and range loss along a branch. I was wondering how these probabilities scaled with range size i.e. if a species is present in area A+B, is the probability of extirpation at any one point in time e(A) +e(B) ? or is it still just e, with 50% probability that it will be extirpated from one or the other? Or is the answer different depending on whether you're using diva, dec or bayarea?


Thanks


Neil

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] d and e parameters
parts:
Hi!

So, d and e are just the d and e from the DEC model of Ree & Smith 2008, see that paper for the rate matrix that is used.

On Sat, Sep 8, 2018 at 9:37 PM, neil brocklehurst <neil_...@hotmail.co.uk> wrote:

Dear Nick

I had a bit of a basic question about the precise nature of the d and e parameters. In your publications/thesis you describe these as rates of range addition and range loss along a branch. I was wondering how these probabilities scaled with range size i.e. if a species is present in area A+B, is the probability of extirpation at any one point in time e(A) +e(B) ?

Technically, the instantaneous probability of going from range AB to range null is 0, because this requires 2 events.

Integrated over 1 time unit, the probability of 

range AB -> range null
...would be lower than either...
A->null
B->null

 As both events have to happen. The exact probability would also depend on d, the number of areas in the analysis, etc.
or is it still just e, with 50% probability that it will be extirpated from one or the other?

The instantaneous rate of loss of A and loss of B are the same, this is true whether they are inside a larger range AB or not. However, integrated over a time unit, the probability of transitioning from AB->A and AB->B might well differ, depending on other parts of the model.
Or is the answer different depending on whether you're using diva, dec or bayarea?

If you mean the 3 likelihood models,

DEC
DIVALIKE
BAYAREALIKE

...which are not precisely identical with the programs DIVA and BayArea...

...then yes, the d/e processes work identically in the three models. The only thing that changes between the three is the cladogenesis processes allowed.

Cheers!
Nick

 


Thanks


Neil

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] d and e parameters
parts: PS: All that said, the accurate inference of "e" is highly problematic, basically pathological, mostly because the null range state is never observed at the tips -- see Massana et al. on BioArxiv...
